sasha: Heads-up: profiler on nightly for Llama-2-70b int8 with TP=4 shows heavy NCCL stall spikes during decode when seq_len>1024. KV-cache scatter spikes seem correlated with all-reduce latency. Anyone else hit this?

maya: ugh, saw something similar on q8m run last week. Do you have counters / perftrace snippets? :thinking_face: 

sasha: pasted below from perf-trace (3 iters around failure):
```
iter 123: allreduce_wait 12.8ms, compute 6.2ms, nvlink_util 0.78, stall_pct 66
iter 124: allreduce_wait 15.4ms, compute 5.9ms, stall_pct 72
kv_scatter_bytes_per_shard 1.2MB
host_mem_copies 3
```

jorge: that stall_pct looks like comm-starvation. Is kernel selection falling back to non-fused matmul for int8 TP shards? Any fp16 kernels used intermittently?

sasha: kernel selector picks int8-quantized matmul + reorder on shard-2 occasionally; other shards use fused int8 kernel. Behavior seems non-deterministic when scale factors differ across shards.

ryan: scaling mismatch across TP shards is a known gotcha — we currently quantize per-tensor but without a deterministic reduction across TP replicas. If scales diverge, some shards trigger reorder/pack kernels and extra memcpy, which amplifies allreduce pressure. PR #1882 tried to coordinate scales but regressed perf.

maya: can you paste the runtime config + callstack markers? Also what's our overlap budget? Could be too small to hide the extra allreduce.

sasha: config + snippet:
```
runtime.tuning.max_overlap_ms=4
tp=4
quant.mode=int8_scale_per_tensor
kv.coalesce=false
```
callstacks show repeated `ncclAllReduce` waits on GPU 2 interleaved with `pack_reorder` on host.

dominique: quick experiment: increase `max_overlap_ms` to 12 and re-run to see if overlap hides it. If stall% drops, we know it's overlap budget related.

sasha: did that — bumping overlap to 12ms lowered visible stall_pct to ~22% on the sample, but overall e2e p50 is still +8% vs fp16 baseline. So overlap helps but doesn't fully recover.

perf-bot: CI perf test 2026-03-17-22: int8-tp4-decoding p50 +7.8% (regression flagged). See perf dashboard.

ryan: sounds like two separate problems: (1) per-shard scale mismatch forcing extra reorder/memcpy + kernel fallback, (2) increased KV scatter frequency creating many small allreduces that increase network overhead. For (2) we should consider coalescing KV updates across micro-batches / tokens.

jorge: agreed. Small allreduces are killers on NVLink/NVSwitch for TP setups. We can try prefix-KV coalescing in the runtime: aggregate writes into a larger tensor before the communication step. Minimal change in CPUID loop.

maya: also add deterministic fallback: if shard scales differ by >2x, do a coordinated normalization (or fallback to fp16 fused kernel) to avoid reorders mid-decode. That reduces non-deterministic kernel churn.

sasha: opening a draft PR with both fixes: coalescing + deterministic scaling fallback to fp16 for outlier shards. Draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2045

maya: nice. Please add perftrace markers around `kv_coalesce_start` / `kv_coalesce_end` and an AB perf test (tp4 int8 decode, seq_len 2048). I'll run smoke on gpu-4-nightly once it's up.

sasha: will do. Also adding a small repro script that toggles `quant.mode` and dumps per-shard scales + kernel picks. Posting here after CI. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: Build 2045-branch:lint OK, unit-tests passed, nightly perf queued.

dominique: if coalescing alone fixes most of the small-allreduce pressure we can land it quickly. Keep the scale-normalization as a follow-up if CI shows regressions.

sasha: thanks all — I'll post updated perftrace + a short summary once jobs finish.
